newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico sets Toluca area for natgas distribution.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sets Toluca area for natgas distribution.

text.p: A key industrial region in the state of Mexico was designated as a site for future natural gas distribution, the Energy Regulatory Commission said in the daily gazette Monday.

Gas distribution rights in the city of Toluca, about 50 kms (30 miles) west of Mexico City, and outlying towns, will be auctioned off to private companies, although the commission did not specify when.
Natural gas enters the region through the southeast by state-owned Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) 10-inch/254 mm ducts, which the commission said are insufficient for the industrial needs of the region.

"Actual gas consumption in the metropolitan region is about five billion kilocalories and the demand for other fuel by the population and industrial, electrical, commercial and other sectors is estimated at more than 12 billion kilocalories per day," the gazette said.
Metropolitan Toluca had a population of 886,263, as of Mexico's 1990 census, with an annual growth rate of four percent. The area represents about two percent of the national gross domestic product.
In efforts to build the necessary infrastructure for natural gas, a cleaner fuel than the liquid petroleum gas dominant in the area, the government is accepting bids for natural gas distribution.
Bidding is in process for distribution in Chihuahua and Sonora states and a concession has been granted in Mexicali.
-- Timna Tanners, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7903 (c) Reuters Limited 1996
